title: A strong magnetic field in the jet base of a supermassive black hole
question: Can Faraday rotation be detected at the jet base of PKS 1830-211 with ALMA, and what does the rotation measure imply for the magnetic field strength?

evidence.quote: a powerful gravitationally-lensed AGN located at a redshift of $z = 2.5$ (cite: lid99)

what.value: Parsec-scale AGN core magnetic fields of ~0.05-0.10 G used for comparison

evidence.quote: where the derived magnetic fields have been independently measured to be $\simeq 0.05-0.10$ Gauss (cite: Gabuzda4; Gabuzda5)

recipe.goal: Measure flux-density ratios of lensed images
recipe.method: Fit XX and YY visibilities separately with a two-component model, bypassing imaging
Rpol = 1/2 (R_XX/R_YY - 1) with errors by standard propagation from fit covariance matrix
Least-squares fit of Rpol vs lambda^2 and parallactic angle with a cosine model, for three epochs with quasi-simultaneous 250 and 300 GHz data; 100 GHz data excluded
assumptions: RMs and fractional polarization wavelength dependence similar for both lensed images, so p_dif and alpha are constant

recipe.goal: Convert to rest frame and infer magnetic field
recipe.method: RM_true = (1+z)^2 RM_obs; compare with RM integral n B dl and parsec-scale AGN core RMs to bound B

evidence.quote: whereas between 0.8 and 1.6 mm$^2$ it is $70\times 10^{-3}$ mm$^{-2}$

not_stated_but_needed: Source models (number of components) used in UVMULTIFIT
Initial guesses and parameter bounds of the Rpol fit
How the data were split into parallactic angle segments
Which executions belong to which project code
score_reason: Data and tables of Rpol are given and the method is clear, but calibration, source model and fit details are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Rpol per epoch is tabulated and the cosine fit is simple, so RM values can be reproduced from the tables, though the archive data reprocessing needs missing details.
